safety_verdicts.content: Urinary symptoms include noticing some pink-colored urine, but no frank hematuria or dysuria.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes pink urine and denies dysuria, but does not capture the Gold statement of no frank hematuria (patient was uncertain about blood in transcript).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Hematuria (even suspected) can signal important alternate diagnoses (e.g., stone, more complicated UTI), so documenting it accurately matters. However, the note still captures the key finding of pink urine and lack of dysuria, so the incremental risk from omitting “no frank hematuria/uncertainty” is limited.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, headaches, or visual symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated captures denial of SOB, palpitations, headache, and visual changes, but does not include denial of chest pain.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting a denial of chest pain slightly degrades the completeness of the review of systems and could prompt redundant follow-up questions or leave ambiguity for later readers. In this presentation focused on lower abdominal pain/urinary symptoms, it is unlikely to change management or create direct clinical harm.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document a specific 24–48 hour review window can delay reassessment if symptoms do not improve, which is important when serious abdominal or urinary pathology remains possible. Delayed follow-up could worsen outcomes by postponing escalation of care and further evaluation.
